meta.note: Distilled by subagent from video transcripts (rolling, Aug 2026). Visibility-only: takes never move projections; adjustments require player_adjust.json with documented reasons. Prune takes AND facts older than ~3 weeks. Each take carries a separate 'mechanism' field — audit the mechanism independently of the conclusion before repeating it (see expert_methods.md -> Mechanism audit). direction 'contested' = the sources, or the FF hosts internally, disagree.

Team grooming him as a three-down back (new pass-catching reports), Ekeler gone, only Rachaad White as competition, in what should be a top rushing offense — yet ADP is RB37, lower than last year.

24% overall / 40% red-zone target share with no proven WR competition — a 150+ target ceiling that could break the TE reception record; FF have him firmly TE1 over McBride.
Looked good and is confirmed in the Packers' base two-WR sets.
takes.mechanism: Preseason two-WR-set usage confirmed Golden alongside Christian Watson.

takes.mechanism: He was fantasy WR3 over the first month of 2025 and led the Bears in first-read targets and first-read share under pressure; the collapse dates entirely to the week-9 foot injury, so the hierarchy should reassert under Ben Johnson.

takes.why: Beat reports say ~50/50 rushing split with Kyren Williams in the NFL's #1 yardage offense, projected ~900 total yards, and inherits a top-5 role if Kyren's ankle/foot history flares — round 8-9 price.

McDaniel has led the NFL in pre-snap motion five straight years and McConkey is #6 in YPRR on motion plays; Keenan Allen's 122 targets left; healthy weeks 5-10 he was a top-12 WR — round-4 cost.
Top-12 QB in every healthy season with 400-600 rushing-yard upside, now with Jefferson/Addison/Hockenson under O'Connell — going round 10-11 because of a camp 'battle' he's winning.
May be his own tier at running back, above the rest of the RB1 group.
22.4 ppg in starts with 80%+ snaps (QB2 behind only Allen) with an 800-1,000 rush-yard ceiling; healthy year 3 with Diggs added — near-QB1 upside ~50 picks after Allen.
QB7 then QB6 in his first two seasons, led the NFL in pass attempts, added Waddle — yet priced QB15; tough early schedule means shootouts, which help QBs.
Not fading him — the groin reads as a 2-3 week precaution and he should be ready for week 1.
takes.mechanism: Non-contact injury, no need for him in the preseason, and a 2-3 week heal carries low re-injury risk (per Jeff Mueller).

takes.why: Cannot be started week 1 in any world; the pick is wasted.
takes.mechanism: Canales explicitly framed week 1 as a committee contingent on Hubbard being healthy, and his RB talk historically trends toward more committee than he first signals.

takes.why: DIRECT CONFLICT: Sal fades hard at RB30/pick 75 (peak hype); Andy is 'very pro Brooks, big time' and says drafting Hubbard now is setting a pick on fire.
takes.mechanism: Sal: Hubbard's hamstring is only week-to-week so the backfield splits on his return, and Brooks is two ACLs deep on a bad offense. FF: Canales said week 1 is a committee IF Hubbard is good to go — a downgrade from 'he's our guy' — and Brooks actually started and played in preseason.

takes.why: Elite talent but re-aggravated a chronic hamstring (now the other one) with a ~2-month timeline and likely PUP; draft only with an IR spot — and it caps Tyler Shough's ceiling.
Jason's official bust pick of the year.
takes.mechanism: Three separable claims: (1) offense/O-line downgrade JAX→NO; (2) 4 TDs on 26 inside-10 carries (15%) and 2 on 12 inside the 5 — a genuine red-zone efficiency flag; (3) 6 receiving TDs on 36 catches is a 3-player, 25-year outlier and 43% of his points came from TDs, so the baseline must regress. Kamara re-absorbs passing-down work by ~week 3.

takes.why: Flatly not draftable right now despite last year's breakout rookie profile.
takes.mechanism: Did not start with the first team and played zero snaps on the first two drives with Herbert, entering only with the backups — because he cannot block, and McDaniel's system requires blocking TEs, which is why they signed Charlie Kolar.

takes.why: Kept a 23% target share and 30% of red-zone targets through last year's injury mess; healthy Daniels plus a new OC moving him around make round 5 a two-round discount.

takes.mechanism: Top-five points-per-game receiver last season whenever on the field, currently going in round 3 — a 6th-round keeper is real surplus.

Mild caution at a 7th-8th round price — he needs outside snaps in 2-WR sets to justify it.
takes.mechanism: On the starters' only drive he lined up in the slot, and Treylon Burks looks like a real WR3 on a team expected to play heavy 11 personnel. A slot-only role caps the ceiling.

strategy_notes.note: Anchor with elite RBs: two RBs in your first three picks (reliability, not breakout swings) — RBs fly early this year and the position is barren by round 5.

The RB dead zone is back — RB24 now costs a 5th-round pick (a 7th in 2024) — grab two elite backs in the first 3-4 rounds and refuse to pay for middling RB2/3s (Etienne, Montgomery, Warren, Pollard all priced above projection).
Elite QB prices are the cheapest in years — Lamar a full round-plus cheaper than last year's QB2; Burrow (rd 5) / Daniels and Hurts (rd 6) are legitimate value even for late-round-QB drafters.
Wait on QB in 1QB: Allen is the lone QB priced in round 2 while Daniels/Hurts/Maye deliver comparable upside ~50 picks later; rounds 10-11 are the last window for Kyler/Mahomes/Purdy types.
Avoid RBs on bad teams: backs on sub-7-win teams hit ADP only ~30% of the time; 2026 teams that are underdogs in 3+ of their first 4 (ARI, CLE, IND, LV, MIA, NYJ, DEN) create uphill starts.
Don't stash day-2/3 rookie WRs early (48%/30% snaps, 2-4 targets through week 6) — only first-round rookies start day one; spend late picks on backup RBs whose value transfers predictably.

The old-WR cliff is the worst bet on the board: the 10 oldest drafted players beat ADP just 30% of the time and old WRs only 21% — this year that's Adams and Evans — with encore-effect exceptions (Henry, Kelce, Stafford).

Tight end is elite-or-punt: pay for Bowers/McBride/Loveland/Warren or wait for late profiles with 17%+ target share and 15%+ air-yard share (Likely, Goedert, Kincaid, Juwan Johnson) — mid-round TEs waste RB/WR upside picks.

Stefon Diggs — 170 vacated targets; late-round steal.
Bhayshul Tuten — Etienne's vacated touches with glowing camp reports.
Camp-buzz rookies confirmed by preseason usage: De'Zhaun Stribling (SF), Caleb Douglas (MIA), Pat Bryant (DEN).
